name: Chapter 2: Structure of Atom
description: Subatomic particles, Thomson and Rutherford models, EM radiation, photoelectric effect, Bohr model, de Broglie, uncertainty, quantum numbers, orbitals and configurations

cards.term: Origin of the word "atom"?
cards.definition: Greek "a-tomio": uncut-able, non-divisible

cards.term: What did Dalton’s theory fail to explain (that led to sub-atomic particles)?
cards.definition: Why glass or ebonite gets charged when rubbed with silk or fur

cards.term: What did Faraday’s electrolysis work (1830) suggest?
cards.definition: The particulate nature of electricity

cards.term: Conditions for discharge in a cathode ray tube?
cards.definition: Very low pressure and very high voltage

cards.term: Why a perforated anode and ZnS coating?
cards.definition: Rays pass through the hole and make a bright spot on the phosphorescent ZnS, proving flow from cathode to anode

cards.text: Cathode rays travel from {{c1::cathode to anode}}, in {{c2::straight lines}} without fields, and behave as {{c3::negatively charged}} particles.

cards.term: Do cathode ray properties depend on electrode material or gas?
cards.definition: No: so electrons are a basic constituent of all atoms

cards.term: Everyday device that is a cathode ray tube?
cards.definition: Old television picture tubes (pictures from fluorescence on the screen)

cards.term: Who measured e/mₑ, when, and how?
cards.definition: J.J. Thomson, 1897, balancing perpendicular electric and magnetic fields

cards.term: Thomson’s apparatus: where does the beam hit with only E-field, only B-field, both balanced?
cards.definition: Only electric: A. Only magnetic: C. Balanced: B (undeflected).

cards.text: Deflection of a charged particle increases with its {{c1::charge}} and the {{c2::field strength}}, and decreases with its {{c3::mass}}.

cards.term: Value of e/mₑ?
cards.definition: 1.758820 × 10¹¹ C kg⁻¹

cards.term: Who measured the electron’s charge, and by what experiment?
cards.definition: R.A. Millikan, oil drop experiment (1906–14)

cards.term: Charge on the electron?
cards.definition: −1.602176 × 10⁻¹⁹ C (Millikan got −1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C)

cards.term: How did the oil drops get charged in Millikan’s experiment?
cards.definition: Air was ionised by X-rays; drops picked up charge by colliding with ions

cards.term: Millikan’s key conclusion?
cards.definition: Charge on any drop is an integral multiple of e: \( q = ne \)

cards.term: Three forces on a moving oil drop?
cards.definition: Gravity, electrostatic force and viscous drag

cards.term: Mass of the electron and how obtained?
cards.definition: 9.1094 × 10⁻³¹ kg = e ÷ (e/mₑ), combining Millikan and Thomson

cards.term: Canal rays: how do they differ from cathode rays?
cards.definition: Positive ions their mass and e/m depend on the gas deflected opposite to cathode rays

cards.term: Smallest positive ion from canal rays, and when characterised?
cards.definition: The proton (from hydrogen), 1919

cards.term: Who discovered the neutron, when, how?
cards.definition: Chadwick, 1932, bombarding beryllium with α-particles

cards.term: Properties of fundamental particles

cards.term: Which is heavier, proton or neutron?
cards.definition: Neutron (1.674927 vs 1.6726216 × 10⁻²⁷ kg)

cards.term: Thomson model (1898)?
cards.definition: Sphere (r ≈ 10⁻¹⁰ m) of uniform positive charge with electrons embedded; mass uniform

cards.term: Other names of Thomson’s model?
cards.definition: Plum pudding, raisin pudding or watermelon model

cards.term: What did Thomson’s model explain, and what did it fail?
cards.definition: Explained overall neutrality; failed Rutherford’s scattering results

cards.term: Who discovered X-rays, and properties?
cards.definition: Röntgen, 1895: not deflected by fields, highly penetrating, λ ≈ 0.1 nm

cards.term: Who discovered radioactivity?
cards.definition: Henri Becquerel

cards.term: What are α-particles?
cards.definition: Helium nuclei: 2 units of positive charge, 4 u mass

cards.term: Rutherford’s scattering set-up?
cards.definition: α-particles on a thin gold foil (~100 nm) surrounded by a ZnS screen; with Geiger and Marsden

cards.term: Rutherford: observations → conclusions
cards.definition: Most pass undeflected: Atom is mostly empty space; A few deflected by small angles: Positive charge concentrated in a tiny region; ~1 in 20,000 bounce back (~180°): Nucleus is tiny, dense and positive

cards.term: Radius of atom vs nucleus?
cards.definition: Atom 10⁻¹⁰ m; nucleus 10⁻¹⁵ m (cricket ball nucleus → 5 km atom)

cards.term: Rutherford’s nuclear model in one line?
cards.definition: Tiny dense positive nucleus with electrons revolving in circular orbits, like a solar system

cards.term: Atomic number Z and mass number A?
cards.definition: Z = number of protons (= electrons in neutral atom). A = protons + neutrons (nucleons).

cards.term: Isotopes vs isobars?
cards.definition: Isotopes: same Z, different A (¹²C, ¹³C, ¹⁴C). Isobars: same A, different Z (¹⁴C, ¹⁴N).

cards.term: Isotopes of hydrogen?
cards.definition: Protium ¹H (99.985%), deuterium ²H (0.015%), tritium ³H (trace)

cards.term: Why do isotopes have the same chemistry?
cards.definition: Chemistry depends on electrons (set by Z); neutrons have very little effect

cards.term: Isotones? (extra term)
cards.definition: Same number of neutrons, e.g. ¹⁴C and ¹⁶O (8 n each)

cards.term: p, n, e in ⁸⁰₃₅Br? (Problem 2.1)
cards.definition: p = e = 35, n = 45

cards.term: Species with 18 e, 16 p, 16 n? (Problem 2.2)
cards.definition: ³²₁₆S²⁻ (anion, 2 extra electrons)

cards.term: Why does Rutherford’s model fail on stability?
cards.definition: An orbiting electron is accelerating; by Maxwell it should radiate and spiral into the nucleus in ~10⁻⁸ s

cards.term: Rutherford model’s second drawback?
cards.definition: Says nothing about the distribution and energies of electrons

cards.term: Two developments that led to Bohr’s model?
cards.definition: Dual nature of EM radiation and atomic spectra

cards.term: Who explained EM waves (1870) and who confirmed them?
cards.definition: Maxwell; confirmed by Heinrich Hertz

cards.term: Orientation of E and B fields in an EM wave?
cards.definition: Perpendicular to each other and to the direction of propagation

cards.term: Do EM waves need a medium?
cards.definition: No; they travel in vacuum

cards.term: Uses of EM regions: 10⁶ Hz, 10¹⁰ Hz, 10¹³ Hz, 10¹⁶ Hz?
cards.definition: Radio (broadcast), microwave (radar), IR (heating), UV (sun)

cards.term: Order of EM regions by increasing wavelength.
cards.definition: γ < X < UV < visible < IR < microwave < radio

cards.term: Mnemonic for EM spectrum from long λ to short?
cards.definition: "Raging Martians Invaded Venus Using X-ray Guns": Radio, Micro, IR, Visible, UV, X, Gamma

cards.term: Key wave relations?
cards.definition: \( c = \nu \lambda \) and wavenumber \( \bar{\nu} = \frac{1}{\lambda} \)

cards.term: Units of frequency and wavenumber?
cards.definition: ν: Hz (s⁻¹). Wavenumber: m⁻¹ (SI), cm⁻¹ commonly.

cards.term: Wavelength of Vividh Bharati at 1368 kHz? (Problem 2.3)
cards.definition: λ = c/ν = 219.3 m: radio wave

cards.term: Frequency range of visible light (400–750 nm)?
cards.definition: 7.5 × 10¹⁴ Hz (violet) to 4.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz (red)

cards.term: Wavenumber and frequency of 5800 Å light? (Problem 2.5)
cards.definition: \[\bar{\nu} = 1.724 \times 10^{6}\]m⁻¹; ν = 5.172 × 10¹⁴ Hz

cards.text: Phenomena classical wave theory could not explain: {{c1::black-body radiation}}, the {{c2::photoelectric effect}}, heat capacity of solids vs T, and {{c3::line spectra}} of atoms.

cards.term: What is a black body?
cards.definition: An ideal body that absorbs and emits all frequencies; approximated by a cavity with a tiny hole (or carbon black)

cards.term: Black-body curve: what happens as T rises?
cards.definition: Intensity rises and the peak shifts to shorter wavelength (red → white → blue)

cards.term: Planck’s quantum theory (1900)?
cards.definition: Energy is emitted/absorbed in discrete packets (quanta): \( E = h\nu \)

cards.term: Planck’s constant?
Staircase analogy for quantisation? (intuition)
cards.definition: You can stand on any step but never between steps: E = 0, hν, 2hν, … nhν

cards.term: Photoelectric effect: who observed it first, and metals used?
cards.definition: H. Hertz, 1887; K, Rb, Cs

cards.term: Einstein’s photoelectric equation?
cards.definition: \[h\nu = h\nu_0 + \frac{1}{2} m_e v^2\](W₀ = hν₀ is the work function)

cards.term: Why can bright red light not eject electrons from K, but dim yellow can?
cards.definition: Red ν < ν₀ (5.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz for K); each photon too weak. Intensity only adds more photons, not more energy per photon.

cards.term: Lowest work function among Li, Na, K, Mg, Cu, Ag (Table 2.2)?
cards.definition: K (2.25 eV); highest Cu (4.8 eV)

cards.term: Energy of 1 mol photons at 5 × 10¹⁴ Hz? (Problem 2.6)
cards.definition: 199.5 kJ mol⁻¹

cards.term: Photons emitted per second

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Problem 2.7

100 W bulb, λ = 400 nm. Photons per second?

E = hc/λ; number = power ÷ E.
  1. E = (6.626×10⁻³⁴)(3×10⁸)/(400×10⁻⁹)
  2. = 4.969 × 10⁻¹⁹ J
  3. ?
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Problem 2.7

100 W bulb, λ = 400 nm. Photons per second?

E = hc/λ; number = power ÷ E.
  1. E = (6.626×10⁻³⁴)(3×10⁸)/(400×10⁻⁹)
  2. = 4.969 × 10⁻¹⁹ J
  3. n = 100 / 4.969×10⁻¹⁹ = 2.012 × 10²⁰ s⁻¹

cards.term: Threshold wavelength of sodium
cards.definition: 517 nm

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Problem 2.8

300 nm on Na; KE = 1.68 × 10⁵ J/mol. Work function, λ₀?

hν = W₀ + KE
  1. E(1 mol photons) = 3.99 × 10⁵ J/mol
  2. W₀ = 3.99 − 1.68 = 2.31 × 10⁵ J/mol = 3.84 × 10⁻¹⁹ J per e⁻
  3. ?
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Problem 2.8

300 nm on Na; KE = 1.68 × 10⁵ J/mol. Work function, λ₀?

hν = W₀ + KE
  1. E(1 mol photons) = 3.99 × 10⁵ J/mol
  2. W₀ = 3.99 − 1.68 = 2.31 × 10⁵ J/mol = 3.84 × 10⁻¹⁹ J per e⁻
  3. λ₀ = hc/W₀ = 517 nm (green)

cards.term: Handy shortcut: photon energy in eV from λ in nm? (trick)
cards.definition: \[E(eV) \approx \frac{1240}{\lambda(nm)}\]

cards.term: When does light show wave vs particle behaviour?
cards.definition: Wave while propagating (interference, diffraction); particle when interacting with matter

cards.term: Continuous vs line spectrum?
cards.definition: Continuous: all wavelengths merge (white light, rainbow). Line: only specific wavelengths, from gaseous atoms.

cards.term: Which colour deviates least through a prism?
cards.definition: Red (longest λ); violet deviates most

cards.term: Emission vs absorption spectrum?
cards.definition: Emission: bright lines from excited sample. Absorption: dark lines in a continuous spectrum; the photographic negative.

cards.term: Why are line spectra called atomic "fingerprints"?
cards.definition: Each element has a unique line spectrum

cards.term: Elements discovered by spectroscopy?
cards.definition: Rb, Cs, Tl, In, Ga, Sc; He was found in the sun

cards.term: Early user of line spectra to identify elements?
cards.definition: Robert Bunsen

cards.term: Rydberg formula for hydrogen?
Table 2.3 · Hydrogen spectral series
Mnemonic for the hydrogen series (n₁ = 1 to 5)?
cards.definition: "Lazy Boys Prefer Bed Pillows": Lyman, Balmer, Paschen, Brackett, Pfund

cards.term: Only hydrogen series in the visible region?
cards.definition: Balmer (n₁ = 2)

cards.term: Max number of spectral lines when an electron falls from level n to 1? (JEE)
Bohr’s quantisation condition?
cards.definition: \[m_e v r = n \frac{h}{2\pi}\]

cards.term: Radius of nth Bohr orbit (hydrogen-like)?
Energy of nth orbit (hydrogen-like)?
What does the negative sign in Eₙ mean?
cards.definition: The bound electron has lower energy than a free electron at rest (E = 0 at n = ∞)

cards.term: Energy of H electron at n = 2?
cards.definition: −0.545 × 10⁻¹⁸ J (= −3.4 eV)

cards.term: How do velocity and radius change with Z and n?
cards.definition: Velocity ∝ Z/n; radius ∝ n²/Z

cards.term: Bohr’s ΔE for a transition?
cards.definition: \[\Delta E = 2.18 \times 10^{-18} \left( \frac{1}{n_i^2} - \frac{1}{n_f^2} \right)\]J

cards.term: Absorption vs emission in Bohr’s model?
cards.definition: Absorption: nf > ni, ΔE positive. Emission: ni > nf, energy released.

cards.term: Frequency and wavelength for H transition n = 5 → 2? (Problem 2.10)
cards.definition: ν = 6.91 × 10¹⁴ Hz, λ = 434 nm (Balmer, visible)

cards.term: Energy and radius of first orbit of He⁺? (Problem 2.11)
cards.definition: E = −8.72 × 10⁻¹⁸ J; r = 26.45 pm

cards.term: Correction: NCERT calls 2.18 × 10⁻¹⁸ J the "Rydberg constant". Precise term?
cards.definition: That is the Rydberg energy (hcR); the Rydberg constant itself is 109677 cm⁻¹ for H

cards.text: Bohr’s model fails to explain: the {{c1::fine (doublet) structure}} of H lines, spectra of {{c2::multi-electron atoms}}, the {{c3::Zeeman}} (magnetic) and {{c4::Stark}} (electric) effects, and {{c5::chemical bonding}}.

cards.term: de Broglie relation (1924)?
cards.definition: \[\lambda = \frac{h}{mv} = \frac{h}{p}\]

cards.term: Experimental proof of electron waves, and its use?
cards.definition: Electron diffraction; used in the electron microscope (~15 million ×)

cards.term: Why don’t we notice the wave nature of a cricket ball?
cards.definition: Large mass → λ far too small to detect

cards.term: λ of a 0.1 kg ball at 10 m/s? (Problem 2.12)
cards.definition: 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ m

cards.term: λ of electron with KE = 3.0 × 10⁻²⁵ J? (Problem 2.13)
cards.definition: v = 812 m/s; λ = 896.7 nm

cards.term: de Broglie λ from kinetic energy (shortcut)?
cards.definition: \( \lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}} \); for an electron through V volts, λ ≈ \( \frac{1.227}{\sqrt{V}} \) nm

cards.term: "Mass" of a 3.6 Å photon? (Problem 2.14)
cards.definition: m = h/λc = 6.135 × 10⁻²⁹ kg

cards.term: Heisenberg uncertainty principle (1927)?
cards.definition: \[\Delta x \cdot \Delta p_x \geq \frac{h}{4\pi}\]exact position and momentum cannot both be known

cards.term: Why can’t we "see" an electron without disturbing it? (intuition)
cards.definition: Light of λ smaller than the electron has huge momentum and knocks the electron away

cards.term: Main implication of the uncertainty principle?
cards.definition: Rules out definite paths or trajectories for electrons; we speak of probability

cards.term: Δv for an electron if Δx = 10⁻⁸ m?
cards.definition: ≈ 5.79 × 10³ m/s: too large for fixed Bohr orbits

cards.term: Δv of an electron located within 0.1 Å? (Problem 2.15)
cards.definition: Δv = h/(4π m Δx) = 5.79 × 10⁶ m/s

cards.term: Δx for a 40 g golf ball at 45 m/s, 2% error? (Problem 2.16)
cards.definition: 1.46 × 10⁻³³ m: meaningless for large objects

cards.term: Two reasons for failure of the Bohr model?
cards.definition: Ignores dual behaviour of electrons; contradicts the uncertainty principle (defined orbits)

cards.term: Who developed quantum mechanics (1926)?
cards.definition: Heisenberg and Schrödinger independently

cards.term: Schrödinger equation form?
cards.definition: \[\hat{H} \psi = E \psi\](Ĥ = Hamiltonian operator)

cards.term: What is an atomic orbital?
cards.definition: The wave function ψ of an electron in an atom

cards.term: Physical meaning of ψ and of |ψ|²?
cards.definition: ψ has no physical meaning; |ψ|² = probability density (always positive)

cards.term: Why do multi-electron orbital energies depend on n and l, not n alone?
cards.definition: Electron–electron repulsion and shielding

cards.term: Orbit vs orbital?
cards.definition: Orbit: definite circular path (Bohr), 2n² e⁻. Orbital: 3D region of probability, max 2 e⁻.

cards.term: The four quantum numbers
cards.definition: n (principal): Shell; size and (mainly) energy; l (azimuthal): Subshell; shape; mₗ (magnetic): Orientation in space; mₛ (spin): Spin orientation, +½ or −½

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Quantum numbers

What does it tell?

n (principal)?
l (azimuthal)?
mₗ (magnetic)?
mₛ (spin)?
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Quantum numbers

What does it tell?

n (principal)Shell; size and (mainly) energy
l (azimuthal)Subshell; shape
mₗ (magnetic)Orientation in space
mₛ (spin)Spin orientation, +½ or −½

cards.text: For a given n, l = {{c1::0 to n − 1}}; for a given l, mₗ = {{c2::−l … 0 … +l}}, i.e. {{c3::2l + 1}} values.

cards.term: Shell letters for n = 1, 2, 3, 4?
cards.definition: K, L, M, N

cards.term: Subshell letters for l = 0, 1, 2, 3?
cards.definition: s, p, d, f

cards.term: Number of orbitals in shell n; max electrons?
cards.definition: n² orbitals; 2n² electrons

cards.term: Orbitals in n = 3? (Problem 2.17)
cards.definition: 1 + 3 + 5 = 9
2p, 4s, 5f, 3d

cards.term: Which of these is impossible: 1p, 2s, 2d, 3f, 3p? (classic)
cards.definition: 1p, 2d, 3f (l must be < n)

cards.term: Who proposed electron spin, and when?
cards.definition: Uhlenbeck and Goudsmit, 1925

cards.term: What led to the fourth quantum number?
cards.definition: Lines appearing as doublets and triplets in multi-electron spectra

cards.term: Correction: NCERT says the electron "spins around its own axis like the earth". Accurate?
cards.definition: Not literally: spin is an intrinsic quantum angular momentum; the spinning-top picture is only an analogy

cards.term: ψ and ψ² vs r for 1s and 2s?
cards.definition: 1s: max at nucleus, falls off. 2s: falls to zero (a node) then rises again

cards.term: Number of radial nodes formula?
cards.definition: n − l − 1 (ns has n − 1)

cards.term: Number of angular nodes; total nodes?
cards.definition: Angular = l; total = n − 1

cards.term: Radial and angular nodes in 3p and 4d? (JEE)
cards.definition: 3p: 1 radial, 1 angular. 4d: 1 radial, 2 angular.

cards.term: What is a boundary surface diagram?
cards.definition: Surface of constant |ψ|² enclosing ~90% probability of finding the electron

cards.term: Why not draw a 100% boundary surface?
cards.definition: |ψ|² is never zero at any finite distance

cards.term: Shape and size order of s orbitals?
cards.definition: Spherical; 4s > 3s > 2s > 1s

cards.term: Shape of p orbitals, and nodal plane of pz?
cards.definition: Two lobes (dumbbell) along x, y, z; pz has the xy-plane as nodal plane

cards.term: Is there a simple link between mₗ = −1, 0, +1 and px, py, pz?
cards.definition: No

cards.term: Lowest n with d orbitals, and their names?
cards.definition: n = 3; dxy, dyz, dxz, dx²−y², dz²

cards.term: Which d orbital has a different shape?
cards.definition: dz² (dumbbell with a ring/doughnut); all five 3d are degenerate

cards.term: Which d orbitals have lobes along the axes?
cards.definition: dx²−y² and dz²; the other three lie between axes

cards.term: Energy order in the hydrogen atom?
cards.definition: Depends on n only: 1s < 2s = 2p < 3s = 3p = 3d < …

cards.term: What are degenerate orbitals?
cards.definition: Orbitals of the same energy

cards.term: Define effective nuclear charge.
cards.definition: Net positive charge felt by an outer electron after shielding by inner electrons (Zeff·e)

cards.term: Shielding order within a shell?
cards.definition: s > p > d > f (s electrons penetrate closest to the nucleus)

cards.term: The (n + l) rule?
cards.definition: Lower (n + l) → lower energy; if equal, lower n is lower

cards.term: Which is lower: 4s or 3d? 4f or 6p?
cards.definition: 4s (4+0 < 3+2). 4f (7, lower n than 6p also 7).

cards.term: Order E₂s(H), E₂s(Li), E₂s(Na), E₂s(K)?
cards.definition: E₂s(H) > E₂s(Li) > E₂s(Na) > E₂s(K): energy falls as Z rises

cards.term: Aufbau principle?
cards.definition: In the ground state, orbitals are filled in order of increasing energy ("aufbau" = building up)

cards.term: Standard filling order?
cards.definition: 1s, 2s, 2p, 3s, 3p, 4s, 3d, 4p, 5s, 4d, 5p, 6s, 4f, 5d, 6p, 7s

cards.term: Pauli exclusion principle (1926)?
cards.definition: No two electrons in an atom can have the same four quantum numbers; an orbital holds 2 e⁻ of opposite spin

cards.term: Hund’s rule of maximum multiplicity?
cards.definition: Electrons pair in a subshell only after each orbital is singly occupied (same spin)

cards.term: Pairing starts with which electron in p, d, f?
cards.definition: 4th, 6th and 8th

cards.term: Mnemonic for Hund’s rule? (intuition)
cards.definition: "Bus seat rule": passengers take an empty double seat before sitting next to someone

cards.term: Advantage of orbital (box) diagrams over spdf notation?
cards.definition: Shows all four quantum numbers (including spin)

cards.term: Core vs valence electrons?
cards.definition: Core: in completely filled inner shells. Valence: in the outermost shell.

cards.term: Configuration of N and O?
cards.definition: N: 1s² 2s² 2p³. O: 1s² 2s² 2p⁴.

cards.term: Configuration of K and why?
cards.definition: [Ar] 4s¹: 4s is lower than 3d

cards.term: Configurations of Cr and Cu?
cards.definition: Cr: [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹. Cu: [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹.

cards.term: Why do Cr and Cu break the aufbau pattern?
cards.definition: Half-filled (d⁵) and fully filled (d¹⁰) subshells have extra stability

cards.term: Where do 4f and 5d get filled?
cards.definition: From lanthanum to mercury

cards.term: Elements after which one are all artificial and short-lived?
cards.definition: Uranium

cards.term: Unpaired electrons in Fe, Fe²⁺, Fe³⁺? (JEE)
cards.definition: 4, 4, 5 (ions lose 4s electrons first)

cards.term: Trap: which electrons leave first when a transition metal ionises?
cards.definition: 4s (outermost n), even though they filled first

cards.text: Half-filled and fully filled subshells are extra stable because of {{c1::symmetrical distribution}} of electrons and maximum {{c2::exchange energy}}.

cards.term: What is exchange energy?
cards.definition: Energy released when electrons of the same spin in degenerate orbitals exchange positions

cards.term: Number of exchanges in d⁵?
cards.definition: 10 (4 + 3 + 2 + 1): maximum

cards.term: Link between exchange energy and Hund’s rule?
cards.definition: Parallel spins maximise exchanges → the basis of Hund’s rule

cards.term: Who discovered what
cards.definition: Electron e/m: J.J. Thomson, 1897; Electron charge: Millikan (oil drop); Neutron: Chadwick, 1932; Nucleus: Rutherford (α-scattering); Quantum theory: Planck, 1900; Matter waves: de Broglie, 1924
